results.name: lag1_response_dependence
results.description: P(yes | previous consecutive trial yes) minus P(yes | previous trial no), using rows where trial_index increments by 1 from the previous row; observed above the replicate mean means people perseverate on their prior response (sequential dependence the independent-trial model lacks).

results.name: far_outside_range_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for targets outside the examples' [min,max] range and more than 25 from the nearest example; observed above the replicate mean means the model under-produces far-outside yeses (floor too low), below means it over-produces them.
results.code:
# name: far_outside_range_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for targets outside the examples' [min,max] range and more than 25 from the nearest example; observed above the replicate mean means the model under-produces far-outside yeses (floor too low), below means it over-produces them.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = ((t < lo) | (t > hi)) & (dist > 25)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: mixed_parity_set_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets on multi-example sets containing both odd and even numbers and no shared last digit (no obvious rule); observed above the replicate mean means people generalize more broadly from rule-less sets than the model, below means more conservatively.
results.code:
# name: mixed_parity_set_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets on multi-example sets containing both odd and even numbers and no shared last digit (no obvious rule); observed above the replicate mean means people generalize more broadly from rule-less sets than the model, below means more conservatively.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    par = np.mod(ex, 2)
    has_odd = np.nansum(par == 1, axis=1) > 0
    has_even = np.nansum(par == 0, axis=1) > 0
    d = np.mod(ex, 10)
    same_digit = np.all(np.isnan(d) | (d == d[:, [0]]), axis=1)
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & has_odd & has_even & ~same_digit & ~isex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: wide_range_interior_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the [min,max] of multi-example sets spanning at least 30; observed above the replicate mean means people interpolate (interval-like generalization) more than the model, below means less.
results.code:
# name: wide_range_interior_yes_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets strictly inside the [min,max] of multi-example sets spanning at least 30; observed above the replicate mean means people interpolate (interval-like generalization) more than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    lo, hi = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 2) & (hi - lo >= 30) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & ~isex
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())

results.name: shared_last_digit_contrast
results.description: Among multi-example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that last digit minus yes rate for targets without it; observed above the replicate mean means people follow the last-digit rule more sharply than the model, below means less sharply.
results.code:
# name: shared_last_digit_contrast
# description: Among multi-example sets whose examples all share a last digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that last digit minus yes rate for targets without it; observed above the replicate mean means people follow the last-digit rule more sharply than the model, below means less sharply.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(ex), axis=1)
    d = np.mod(ex, 10)
    first = d[:, 0]
    same = np.all(np.isnan(d) | (d == first[:, None]), axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    isex = (ex == t[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    match = np.mod(t, 10) == first
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    a = same & ~isex & match
    b = same & ~isex & ~match
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: late_minus_early_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials in the second half of the session (trial_index >= median) minus the first half; nonzero observed vs a near-zero replicate mean means response bias drifts over the session (positive = growing yes-bias), which the stationary model cannot produce.

results.name: example_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below the replicate mean means the model's guessing ceiling is too high (people reject examples more), above means people endorse examples more than the lapse allows.

results.name: single_example_generalization_rate
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets when only one example is shown; observed above the replicate mean means people generalize more broadly from a single example than the model's size-principle posterior, below means more narrowly.
results.code:
# name: single_example_generalization_rate
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets when only one example is shown; observed above the replicate mean means people generalize more broadly from a single example than the model's size-principle posterior, below means more narrowly.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    one = ~s.str.contains(",").to_numpy()
    num = pd.to_numeric(s.str.split(",").str[0], errors="coerce").to_numpy()
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy()
    m = one & (num != t)
    if m.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(df["rating"].to_numpy()[m].mean())
